cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 45 on-track passes, 28 pit stops, 3 cars that never finished, 1 safety car, 2 virtual safety cars.

cards.title: 22 places changed hands on track before the first lap was done
cards.text: 22 cars into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks.
bullets: Hadjar gained the most by the end of it, 6 places
cards.note: The safety car came out on the opening lap. Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the race.

cards.title: Every gap on track, erased
cards.text: The field bunches up behind the safety car, and whatever anybody had built is gone.
bullets: Antonelli was leading when it came out
He stayed out while Hadjar, Bearman, Perez and 2 others stopped under it
Neutralised until lap 4
cards.note: This early, nobody had a lead to lose. What it did do was hand a cheap stop to whoever was ready to take one.

cards.title: 5 incidents looked at
cards.text: Every one of them logged by race control during the race.
bullets: First up, lap 1: Hamilton and Russell, causing a collision
1 ended in a penalty, 3 in no further action and 1 left for after the race

cards.title: Russell is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 1 of 44, in a Mercedes.
bullets: Started P3
Race control logged an incident with Hamilton and Russell at Turn 6 on lap 1

cards.title: Hadjar starts P21. Where does he finish?
cards.text: 44 laps to make up ground from there.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 6 times
cards.text: Race control waves a yellow for anything on or near the track that should not be there.
bullets: A yellow means slow down and do not overtake in that part of the track
Track sectors 7 and 15 saw 4 each, the most of anywhere

cards.title: 6 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 6 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: Early on, with full tanks and the order still settling.

cards.title: 9 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track, and the lap simply stops counting if you leave it.
bullets: Antonelli lost 2 that way, more than anybody
cards.note: Keep doing it and it turns into a penalty.

cards.title: 6 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 5 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: Early on, with full tanks and the order still settling.

cards.title: Lap 8: contact between Leclerc and Piastri at Turn 5. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and it lands on your desk. Same call the stewards had to make.

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the race on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if there is no stop left. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards took no further action.

cards.title: 1 penalty handed out
cards.text: Given by the stewards during the race.
bullets: Hamilton: a 5s penalty for causing a collision
cards.note: A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left.

cards.title: Gasly: 5 laps within a second of the car ahead
cards.text: The longest unbroken run like it in the race, from lap 9 to lap 13, at racing speed.
bullets: 1 other driver had a run of five laps or more like it
cards.note: Following closely costs the car downforce and cooks the front tyres, so sitting there is harder than it looks.

cards.title: Track at 34°C at the start, falling to 30°C at the flag
cards.text: Track temperature changes how much grip the tyres find and how fast they wear. No rain was recorded during the race.

cards.title: Gasly: 8 passes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in an Alpine.
bullets: P10 on the grid, P11 at the flag
cards.note: Only moves made on track count, with the car ahead at racing speed.

cards.title: Perez is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 14 of 44, in a Cadillac.
bullets: P21 at the start of lap 13
Started P18
2 on-track passes before it happened
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.kicker: Your call on the pit wall
cards.title: You are Verstappen, 2.1s behind Antonelli and going nowhere. Now what?
cards.text: Stuck behind another car your tyres overheat and the car will not turn. Stopping first gives you clean track for two or three laps, which is the whole trick behind the undercut.

choices.label: Box now and undercut
choices.sub: Fresh tyres, clean air, two laps to make it pay

choices.label: Stay out and overcut
choices.sub: Let him stop first, then push on an empty track

choices.label: Forget strategy, pass him
choices.sub: Send it and take the risk

outcomes.box: You spend about 25s in the lane and come out in traffic, betting that two fast laps on new tyres are worth more than the place you just gave up.
outcomes.wait: You stay on old rubber while he gets new ones, and you need clean air plus a mistake from him to make it work.
outcomes.attack: Passing a car with the same tyres on the same fuel is the hardest thing in the sport, and running into the back of him ends both races.

cards.reveal: Verstappen came in on lap 17, 1 lap after this. He finished P3, Antonelli P1.

cards.title: 28 stops, and the busiest lap saw 7 of them
cards.text: Once one car stops, the cars around it have to answer.
bullets: Busiest single lap was 20, with 7 cars in, 6 of them under the virtual safety car
Shortest time in the pit lane: Albon, 22.6s
Longest: Sainz, 34.8s
cards.note: Pit lane time runs from the entry line to the exit line, stop included.

cards.title: Everybody slows down, nobody bunches up
cards.text: Every car is held to a delta time exactly where it is. The gaps freeze instead of vanishing, which is the whole difference from a real safety car.
bullets: Antonelli was leading when it was called
Stroll took a stop under it
Lifted on lap 18
cards.note: A stop under a VSC costs less than one at racing speed, because everybody else is going slowly too. Cheaper, not free: the leader keeps his gap and the queue behind him keeps its shape.

cards.title: Lawson hit 323 km/h
cards.text: The fastest car in a straight line is often not the fastest car over a lap.
bullets: Lawson did it in a Racing Bulls car
cards.note: Top speed says as much about wing level, and about sitting in somebody's tow, as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Everybody slows down, nobody bunches up
cards.text: Every car is held to a delta time exactly where it is. The gaps freeze instead of vanishing, which is the whole difference from a real safety car.
bullets: Leclerc was leading when it was called
Alonso, Leclerc, Piastri and 4 others stopped under it
Lifted on lap 21
cards.note: A stop under a VSC costs less than one at racing speed, because everybody else is going slowly too. Cheaper, not free: the leader keeps his gap and the queue behind him keeps its shape.

cards.title: Hadjar stopped 3 times
cards.text: Three stops when most of the field made 1.
bullets: In on laps 1, 2 and 20
All of them under a safety car or VSC

cards.title: One of these three does not see the chequered flag. Who?
cards.text: Nothing on the timing screens says it is coming.
cards.reveal: Stroll, on lap 26 of 44. The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Leclerc takes the lead from Norris
cards.text: A pass for the lead, made on track at racing speed.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It usually lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it.
cards.reveal: Norris on lap 44, 1:48.890, in a McLaren.

cards.title: 21 blue flags waved
cards.text: That is how often a lapped car was told to let the leaders through.

cards.title: Stroll is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 26 of 44, in an Aston Martin.
bullets: P20 at the start of lap 25
Started P20
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Stroll was P20 a lap before his race ended on lap 26. Where does he finish if it had not?
cards.text: Nobody can answer this one for certain. You have his own lap times to go on and nothing else.

choices.label: He stays about where he was

cards.reveal: Our read from his own lap times, not a fact. He was lapping 6.12s a lap slower than Antonelli, who went on to win it. With 18 laps left, "he stays about where he was" is the honest guess, and nobody gets to check.

cards.title: Antonelli had the quickest median racing lap
cards.text: No lap 1, no laps in or out of the pits, nothing behind the safety car or the VSC, and the slow outliers trimmed. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Bottas ran one set for 31 laps
cards.text: The longest anybody stayed out on one set.
bullets: On the hards, lap 2 to lap 32
cards.note: Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane. And every lap you stretch is a set of tyres getting slower underneath you.

cards.title: Lawson went the other way: 3 places lost
cards.text: Qualifying promised one thing and the race delivered another.
bullets: P9 on the grid, P12 at the flag
Qualifying rewards whoever can put one lap together. A race asks for 44 of them

cards.title: Hadjar: P21 on the grid, P6 at the flag
cards.text: 15 places gained.
bullets: 6 on-track passes along the way
3 cars that started ahead of him retired

cards.title: Norris: 1:48.890
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all race, in a McLaren.
bullets: Set on lap 44 of 44, late on, where they usually land
By then the fuel is nearly gone and the car is at its lightest
It is worth no points: the bonus point for it was dropped after 2024

cards.title: Antonelli wins it
cards.text: P1 Antonelli · P2 Leclerc · P3 Verstappen.
bullets: After 44 laps, Leclerc crossed the line 1.952s behind
cards.note: Less than the time it takes to read this sentence.

cards.title: How far behind was Leclerc at the flag?
cards.text: 44 laps, 1 hour 25 minutes of racing, and it comes down to this one number.
cards.reveal: 1.952 seconds after 44 laps. A trip down the pit lane took about 25s today, which is 13 times the margin this race was decided by.
